studies.Study: Brinkman MT et al. (2011) [PMID: 20947337] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Consumption of animal products, olive oil and dietary fat and results from the Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk.
studies.Title: Consumption of animal products, olive oil and dietary fat and results from the Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Brinkman MT, Buntinx F, Kellen E, Van Dongen MC, Dagnelie PC, Muls E, Zeegers MP
studies.Population: participants in a Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer
studies.comparison_type: highest versus lowest tertile of olive oil intake

sample_size.excerpt: Dietary data were collected from 200 cases and 386 controls participating in a Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 200 + 386 = 586

cases.excerpt: Dietary data were collected from 200 cases and 386 controls participating in a Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: There was a statistically significant inverse association between olive oil intake and bladder cancer consistent with a linear dose-response relationship: middle versus the lowest tertile (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-0.99) and the highest versus the lowest tertile (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.28-0.78; p-trend = 0.002).

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was a statistically significant inverse association between olive oil intake and bladder cancer consistent with a linear dose-response relationship: middle versus the lowest tertile (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-0.99) and the highest versus the lowest tertile (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.28-0.78; p-trend = 0.002).

comparison.excerpt: the highest versus the lowest tertile (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.28-0.78; p-trend = 0.002)

design.excerpt: a Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer

timing.excerpt: comparing the highest with the lowest tertiles of intake between cases and controls using unconditional logistic regression

continent.excerpt: a Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary data were collected from 200 cases and 386 controls

gender.excerpt: Adjustment was made for age, sex, smoking characteristics, occupational exposures and calorie intake.
